Krasnik New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Krasnik, Poland

Demolished. This is the third of Kraśnik's Jewish cemeteries, established in the first quarter of the 19th century and enlarged twice before reaching its final 1.67-hectare area in 1893. During WWII, the Germans carried out mass executions of about 1,500 people in the cemetery's newest section, burying them in mass graves. After the war, the Jewish community refenced the site with concrete segments, much of which survives today, and exhumed bodies from the surrounding Kraśnik district for reburial here in 1946 and again in 1948. The cemetery was renovated in 2018, though tombstones have continued to be stolen even after the Jewish population left Kraśnik.
